ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Given height h = 500 m, initial velocity u = 0, and gravitational acceleration g = 10 m/s^2. Use the constant-acceleration displacement formula s = ut + (1/2)gt^2. Since u = 0, s = (1/2)gt^2 = 5t^2. For the total fall, 500 = 5t^2, so t^2 = 100 and t = 10 s. For the displacement in the first 1 s, s(1) = 5 × 1^2 = 5 m. For the displacement in the last 1 s, subtract the displacement after 9 s from the displacement after 10 s: s(10) - s(9) = 5(10^2 - 9^2) = 5(100 - 81) = 95 m. Half the total time is 10/2 = 5 s, so the displacement in half the time is s(5) = 5 × 5^2 = 125 m.
